I don't know of any ethical breeder who would inbreed to that extent. My purebred bully has a COI of 14% and these hoarder dogs usually tend to be 25% and higher. Author: @alexlibby5087
Content:
7:00
As a dog trainer/behaviorist who is highly interested in & studying k9 genetics - there are a lot of perpetuated myths about mixed vs pure breeds that I have to correct.
Better education will hopefully help the health & function of future dogs.

Anywho
1. Mixed breeds and rescues ARE NOT healthier than purebreeds. The studies that have been done (Texas a&m just did a larger one) do not show a difference in their health - only that a mutts health ailment will likely need more testing to pin down VS purebreeds who develop more predictable health conditions based on breed.

2. Ethical breeders today are working to not only reverse engineer modern breeds damaged by designer breeding; they also track the inbreeding coefficient % in breeding dogs so they do not continue raising the percentage of inbreeding in dogs. 

3. Interesting point for #2 is that mixed breed and shelter dogs do not have a lower inbreeding %; their numbers can and do regularly run just as high as purebreds.

Which ofcourse, whoever bred or dumped the dogs at shelters obviously are not taking great care of their dogs.

There are ethical breeders out there who are genuinely trying to develop breeds with health & function first; it’s important they get emphasized as unfortunately the “adopt don’t shop” route has not made a dent in the problem; only that people are often adopting rescue dogs with problems an inexperienced owner can not handle.

Ted talk done/

Author: @scarletamazon3455
Content:
Pups were various jack russell and chihuahua mixes, from what we could see. Poor little guys. A very popular crossbreed at the moment too, so I wonder if it was more of a puppy mill type situation than a typical hoarding. He's certainly not rescuing only these tiny dogs of two specific breeds from the streets, and despite most looking like a Chi/Jack cross, even the crossbreeds are pretty expensive now, so I doubt he's going out and buying them all. I usually avoid animal hoarding videos, since it's so desperately sad. I have a lot of sympathy and time for general hoarders, it's a true mental illness often triggered or worstened by a lot of loss... but there's an element of cruelty to the selfishness behind animal hoarding that makes most of the sympathy dry up. Hoarders that hoard out their own families and raise kids in that environment should also seek help before they get that far, and same for animal hoarders. It might be real mental illness behind the animal hoarding too, but any mental illness is also our own responsibility to manage, and we're still responsible for any harm we inflict on others as a result of our mental health issues. Same applies to hoarders. 

I do love that Ken agreed to getting a bonded pair of cats, because his daughter wanted them so much! And because he wanted to adopt from a shelter, and not buy some fancy hypoallergenic breed, even if that would have been understandable! Just shows his ethics and love for his family. Makes me miss my own daddy all over again. Love and miss you, Dad, rest in peace.
